transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Zhao (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (CTO, Sandstone), Leo Mars (ML Eng), Priyanka Singh (Dir Cloud Ops), Jon Park (SRE)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Sandstone's current stack (OpenAI + self-hosted vLLM edge cases), constraints on data residency and KMS, and whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated/Private fits best. Customer wants parity on outputs with their current Anthropic/OpenAI models, predictable latency, and cost controls.

Topics: migration path, eval parity, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), KV cache and batching tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2/KMS/SSO), pilot scope and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We'll keep this pretty focused — try to surface blockers for a migration.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: Hi, I'm Aisha, CTO at Sandstone. We're running a mix — most prod traffic hits OpenAI for generation, some R&D is on Anthropic and a small fleet running vLLM on-prem for lower-cost batch jobs.
[00:24] Leo Mars: Hey all, Leo here. I'm the ML eng owning the inference stack, I handle vLLM tuning and some TGI experiments.
[00:31] Priyanka Singh: Priyanka, Cloud Ops. Mostly concerned about network, KMS, and compliance.
[00:36] Morgan Chen: Great. Samir?
[00:38] Samir Patel: Samir, SE at Redwood. I'll try to map technical gaps and propose a test plan.
[00:42] [00:45] Morgan Chen: Cool. Aisha, can you describe the pain you're hitting that has you exploring a migration?
[00:52] Aisha Rahman: Yeah, budget and latency unpredictability. OpenAI is great but costs spiking for heavy usage. Our on-prem vLLM is cheaper but parity/quality varies — and scaling ops is gnarly. We want predictable unit economics and a path that doesn't degrade chat UX.
[01:09] Samir Patel: When you say parity do you mean exact token-for-token parity or just consistent UX/latency?
[01:16] Aisha Rahman: UX consistency, not bit-for-bit, but we need same hallucination profile and similar safety behavior. Our eval set is large — like 6k prompts with different failure modes.
[01:26] Leo Mars: Also we have TGI experiments for certain models that we dockerize — quick question: how does Redwood handle TGI/vLLM runtimes?
[01:36] Samir Patel: Good question. Redwood supports model variants commonly used with vLLM/TGI by offering compatible model artifacts and runtime optimizations. There's a compatibility layer — some tokenizers and custom ops need validation. We usually run an eval parity check against your golden set.
[01:49] [02:00] Jon Park: On the infra side, our compliance team requires KMS, customer-managed keys, and audit logs for any private deployment. SOC2 is a must, and data residency for EU subsets. Can Hosted satisfy that?
[02:11] Ellen Zhao: For Hosted, we have SOC2 and region controls; we can also integrate with external KMS in Dedicated/Private. For strict KMS + air-gapped requirements, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the route.
[02:25] Priyanka Singh: If we go Hosted with cross-region data isolation, do we get access to detailed token-level billing? We need to attribute costs to product teams.
[02:33] Morgan Chen: Yes — Console gives token-level breakdowns and per-route cost. We can also provide retention controls and exportable billing CSVs.
[02:39] [03:00] Aisha Rahman: The other challenge is latency SLOs — our customer chat targets 150-200ms p50 for short responses. OpenAI averages 120ms but spikes happen. How deterministic is Redwood for p50/p95?
[03:15] Samir Patel: That target is achievable, depends on model and deployment mode. Dedicated GPU pools with pinned capacity hit stable p50 and p95; Hosted can be consistent too but we might recommend Dedicated for production-critical SLAs. Also batching strategies influence p95 — Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV caching which can reduce cost without hurting p50 if configured properly.
[03:35] Leo Mars: About KV cache — we currently do prefix caching in vLLM; any nuance we should know? Does Redwood preserve token-level cache across requests and instances?
[03:46] Samir Patel: Yes, we support KV cache preservation for session affinity plus autoscaling. There's a tradeoff: cross-instance cache warmup vs stovepipe affinity. We can configure TTLs and cache warming strategies as part of the rollout.
[03:58] [04:15] Priyanka Singh: Security: SSO, RBAC, audit logs — any gaps?
[04:20] Ellen Zhao: We support SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and immutable audit logs in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has standard audit trails but for enterprise audit retention we recommend Dedicated with extended retention add-on.
[04:31] Aisha Rahman: For eval parity we want to run a blind A/B versus OpenAI and Anthropic. How do you do blind evals?
[04:40] Samir Patel: We can set up a side-by-side runner — you provide prompts and metrics; we run both the current provider and a Redwood-hosted variant, returning metric diffs and example outputs. We also tag candidate failure clusters. For safety models, we run policy filters and compare flags as well.
[04:53] [05:00] Leo Mars: Do you support same tokenizers? Our stack uses custom tokenizer tweaks and a pre-tokenization step; mismatches have caused scoring differences before.
[05:09] Samir Patel: We can ingest your tokenizer config and run tokenization diffs. If there are custom ops from TGI, we'll validate or patch. There are occasionally small byte-level differences but we focus on semantic parity.
[05:20] [05:40] Priyanka Singh: Network architecture question: if we choose Dedicated in our VPC, do you peer into our VPC or run a private endpoint? How's egress handled?
[05:48] Morgan Chen: Dedicated supports private endpoints and peering; traffic can remain within your network with optional NAT/Egress controls. For full isolation we do Private deployments where control plane is customer-managed.
[06:00] Jon Park: And monitoring — can we inject our tracing hooks? We want per-request tracing and the ability to sample traces into our observability stack.
[06:08] Samir Patel: Yes, we have tracing hooks, and per-route debug mode. You can stream spans to your tracing backend, or use Redwood's console for sampling and drill-down.
[06:18] [06:35] Aisha Rahman: Cost modeling: what's the main lever? Quantization? Batching? Model choice?
[06:44] Samir Patel: All of the above. Optimize uses quantization profiles and model recommendations per workload; batching and KV cache cut tokens charged. We can run a cost simulation given your qps/seq len distribution.
[06:56] Leo Mars: Quick nit: our R&D uses TGI with LoRA adapters. Can Redwood serve LoRA adapters non-destructively?
[07:05] Samir Patel: We have support for adapters and layering — often we recommend packaging adapters as separate artifacts and applying at load time. We'll want to check compatibility with your TGI build.
[07:13] [07:30] Priyanka Singh: Operational playbooks — if a model node glitches, what's the fallback? We need graceful degradation.
[07:36] Samir Patel: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or replicated capacity in another region. Canary rollouts and A/B routing supported.
[07:45] Aisha Rahman: What about tokenization and eval reproducibility again — we need deterministic outputs for a subset of tests.
[07:53] Samir Patel: Determinism is tricky with non-deterministic sampling. For eval reproducibility we run greedy/beam settings or fixed seeds in our eval harness. We can do the same for your parity tests.
[08:04] [08:20] Jon Park: Any limitations with custom op binaries we ship? We've compiled some CUDA kernels for low-latency ops.
[08:28] Samir Patel: Custom OPS are supported in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we restrict to vetted binaries. If you need exact same binary we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can bring custom builds.
[08:38] Leo Mars: Great. For the pilot, what artifacts do you need from us?
[08:44] Samir Patel: A minimal set: model files or pointers, tokenizer configs, your eval prompt set, a sample traffic profile (qps, seq len dist), and list of golden outputs or metrics.
[08:54] Aisha Rahman: We can share that. We'll also need to sign an NDA before we hand over certain model checkpoints.
[09:01] Ellen Zhao: Understood, we can route NDA to your legal.
[09:06] [09:20] Morgan Chen: Timeline expectations — how soon could we run a short pilot?
[09:26] Samir Patel: If we get artifacts this week, a hosted pilot could spin up in 48 hours; Dedicated/Private leads take longer for infra setup — usually 2-4 weeks.
[09:36] Priyanka Singh: For Dedicated, do we need to commit to reserved capacity? What's the commitment model?
[09:41] Morgan Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual terms. We also offer burst options and a ramp plan for initial months.
[09:48] [10:00] Leo Mars: A potential blocker: we use on-prem GPUs with NCCL networking. Can Redwood integrate with our cluster?
[10:07] Samir Patel: For Private on-prem deployments, yes — we ship the runtime and can integrate with your cluster networking and storage. For Hosted/Dedicated those are Redwood-managed infra in cloud regions.
[10:17] Aisha Rahman: About safety filters — we have a custom safety classifier downstream. Will Redwood's safety policies interfere?
[10:24] Samir Patel: We can disable default filters for your routes or wire in your classifier as a post-process. For Hosted, there are opt-in safety features; Dedicated/Private gives you full control.
[10:35] [10:50] Priyanka Singh: Can we do encryption in transit end-to-end with customer-managed certs?
[10:57] Ellen Zhao: Yes, TLS with client certs and private endpoints supported in Dedicated/Private.
[11:06] Morgan Chen: I'm going to propose a pilot: 48h hosted run that mirrors a subset of your workload for parity checks, then a Dedicated pilot if that looks good. Any objections?
[11:15] Aisha Rahman: Sounds reasonable. We want to validate parity and cost delta on representative traffic.
[11:20] Leo Mars: Also include LoRA adapter behavior and tokenizer diffs in that run.
[11:25] Samir Patel: Noted. We'll include an adapter test and tokenization reports.
[11:30] [11:45] Jon Park: We'll need the security questionnaire and SOC2 docs before pilot.
[11:50] Ellen Zhao: Ellen will share security pack after the meeting.
[11:54] Morgan Chen: Okay last block: pricing — can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated cost per 1M tokens with our seq len mix?
[12:05] Samir Patel: Ballpark only now: Hosted variable pricing, Dedicated ~30-40% lower per-token when amortized on reserved capacity. Exact numbers after we see your qps/seq distribution. We'll send a pricing spreadsheet.
[12:20] Aisha Rahman: Any competitor pitfalls we should watch? We've heard vendor lock-in stories.
[12:26] Morgan Chen: We emphasize portability — model artifacts stay yours, and we support standard runtimes to reduce lock-in.
[12:32] [12:50] Priyanka Singh: Final question: SLA for cold start during autoscale?
[12:58] Samir Patel: Cold starts depend on model size and compilation; we provide warm pools and predictive pre-warming as part of Dedicated. For Hosted we have warm-layers but less control; again Dedicated gives you deterministic behavior.
[13:12] Aisha Rahman: That helps.
[13:15] Morgan Chen: Great. Recap of next steps: I'll send pricing and contract basics; Samir will send benchmark plan and a list of artifacts we need; Ellen will send SOC2 and security pack; Aisha/Priyanka will coordinate on artifacts and timelines.
[13:29] Aisha Rahman: We'll target to get the prompts and sample traffic by Friday.
[13:34] Morgan Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra deep-dive with Jon.

Notes on transcript: occasional recognition errors (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "LoRA" sometimes transcribed as "Laura"), filler words, and speaker label noise where multiple people speak over each other.

End of meeting.
